דבר אחר (14a.17): the palm's one heart -- unattributed alternative
King David, speaker in the Avigail narrative (14a.22-14b.2)
איכא דאמרי (14b.4): the second version of Rav Nachman's saying

props.gloss_en: who are the seven prophetesses? Sarah, Miriam, Devorah, Chana, Avigail, Chulda and Esther

Sarah, as written 'father of Milka and father of Yiska' (Gen 11:29), and R' Yitzchak said: Yiska is Sarah, so called because she saw (sachta) by the holy spirit, as said 'all that Sarah tells you, listen to her voice' (Gen 21:12)
another explanation: Yiska -- for all gazed (sochin) at her beauty

Miriam, as written 'Miriam the prophetess, sister of Aaron' (Ex 15:20) and not of Moses: Rav Nachman in Rav's name -- she prophesied while she was [only] Aaron's sister: my mother is destined to bear a son who will save Israel
when he was born the whole house filled with light; her father kissed her head: my daughter, your prophecy is fulfilled
when they cast him into the river, her father tapped her head: my daughter, where is your prophecy?
this is what is written: 'and his sister stood afar off to know' (Ex 2:4) -- to know what would become of her prophecy
Devorah, as written 'Devorah, a prophetess, wife of Lapidot' (Judg 4:4): what is 'wife of Lapidot'? she made wicks for the Sanctuary
'she sat under the palm' (Judg 4:5) -- why under a palm? R' Shimon ben Avshalom: because of [avoiding] seclusion
another explanation: as the palm has but one heart, so Israel of that generation had but one heart toward their Father in heaven

Chana, as written 'my horn is exalted in the Lord' (1 Sam 2:1): 'my horn', not 'my flask' -- David and Solomon, anointed from a horn, their kingship lasted; Saul and Jehu, anointed from a flask, did not

'there is none holy like the Lord, for there is none besides You (biltecha)' (1 Sam 2:2): Rav Yehuda bar Menashya -- read 'to outlast You (levalotecha)': a man's works outlast him, but the Holy One outlasts His works
'and there is no rock (tzur) like our God' -- no artist (tzayar) like our God: a man paints a form on a wall and cannot put breath and soul in it; the Holy One forms a form within a form
Avigail, as written 'she was riding on the donkey and coming down in the covert of the mountain' (1 Sam 25:20) -- object of the difficulty
Rabba bar Shmuel: concerning blood that comes from the hidden parts
she took blood and showed it to him [David]

David: is blood shown at night? Avigail: are capital cases judged at night? David: he [Naval] is a rebel against the kingdom and need not be judged. Avigail: Saul still lives and your coin has not gone out in the world
David: 'blessed is your discernment and blessed are you who kept me this day from coming into blood' (1 Sam 25:33)
'bloods' implies two! rather, it teaches that she uncovered her leg and he walked by its light three parasangs
David: yield to me! Avigail: 'let this not be a stumbling for you' (1 Sam 25:31)
'this' implies there is another -- the affair of Bat Sheva; and so it ended
as she took leave of him she said: 'and when the Lord deals well with my lord, remember your maidservant' (1 Sam 25:31)
Rav Nachman: this is the folk saying: a woman, while conversing, [takes up] the spindle
some say [he said]: the goose walks bent down, but its eyes roam
Chulda, as written 'and Chilkiyahu the priest and Achikam and Achbor went... to Chulda the prophetess' (2 Kgs 22:14)
the school of Rav in Rav's name: Chulda was Jeremiah's relative, and he did not object to her
the school of R' Sheila: because women are compassionate
R' Yochanan: Jeremiah was not there, for he had gone to bring back the ten tribes

and from where that he brought them back? as written 'for the seller shall not return to what was sold' (Ezek 7:13) -- is it possible that the Jubilee had lapsed and a prophet prophesies that it will lapse? rather, it teaches that Jeremiah brought them back

and Josiah son of Amon reigned over them, as written '...that you have done against the altar in Beit El' (2 Kgs 23:17) -- what had Josiah to do with the altar in Beit El? rather, it teaches that Josiah reigned over them
Rav Nachman: from here -- 'also Judah, a harvest is set for you, when I return the captivity of My people' (Hos 6:11)
the verse: 'on the third day Esther put on royalty' (Esth 5:1) -- 'royal garments' would be expected
rather, the holy spirit clothed her
